properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued August 30 at 1:12PM MDT until August 30 at 4:15PM MDT by NWS Salt Lake City UT
properties.description:
FFWSLC

The National Weather Service in Salt Lake City has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Southwestern Kane County in southern Utah...

* Until 415 PM MDT.

* At 112 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 0.5 and 1 inch of rain
has fallen. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks, streams and
normally dry washes.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Johnson Wash and Johnson Lakes Canyon.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Remain alert for flooding even in locations not receiving rain. Dry
washes, streams, and rivers can become raging killer currents in a
matter of minutes, even from distant rainfall.

Flooding is occurring or is imminent. It is important to know where
you are relative to streams, rivers, or creeks which can become
killers in heavy rains. Campers and hikers should avoid streams or
creeks.

CMAMtext: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 4:15 PM MDT. Avoid flooded areas.
CMAMlongtext: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 4:15 PM MDT. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

properties.areaDesc: Charlotte Harbor and Pine Island Sound
properties.headline: Special Marine Warning issued August 30 at 3:44PM EDT until August 30 at 4:30PM EDT by NWS Tampa Bay Ruskin FL
properties.description:
SMWTBW

The National Weather Service in Ruskin has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Charlotte Harbor and Pine Island Sound...

* Until 430 PM EDT.

* At 344 PM EDT, severe thunderstorms capable of producing
waterspouts were located along a line extending from 16 nm east of
Don Pedro Island to 12 nm east of Boca Grande to 7 nm northeast of
North Captiva Island, moving northwest at 15 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can quickly form and capsize boats, damage
vessels, and create suddenly higher waves. Make sure all
on board are in a secure location and wearing life
jackets. Expect wind gusts in excess of 34 knots,
suddenly higher waves, frequent lightning, and heavy
downpours. Make sure all on board are wearing life
jackets.

* Severe thunderstorms will remain over mainly open waters.
properties.instruction: Move to safe harbor until hazardous weather passes.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued August 30 at 11:53AM MST until August 30 at 2:45PM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
FFWFGZ

The National Weather Service in Flagstaff has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Coconino County in north central Arizona...
Including Colorado River between river miles 0 and 11

* Until 245 PM MST /345 PM MDT/.

* At 1153 AM MST /1253 PM MDT/, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms
producing heavy rain across the warned area from Marble Canyon to
near Lees Ferry. Between 0.5 and 1 inch of rain has fallen.
Additional rainfall amounts of 0.25 to 0.5 inches are possible in
the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
normally dry washes, urban areas, highways, streets and
underpasses.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Marble Canyon, Marble Canyon Airport, Jackass Canyon, Horseshoe
Bend and Lees Ferry.

This includes the following highways...
U.S. Highway 89 between mile markers 543 and 546. the Colorado River
between river miles 0 and 11. U.S. Highway 89A between mile markers
531 and 545.

This includes the following slot canyons...
Cathedral Wash, Cathedral Wash and Jackass Canyon.

This includes the following recreation areas and campgrounds...
Lee's Ferry Campground, Lees Ferry Campground, Paria Beach Camp Site,
Opposite Cathedral Camp Site, Cathedral Wash Camp Site, Jackass Camp
Site, Badger Camp Site, Sandbar Camp Site, Soap Creek Camp Site,
Ferry Swale Camp Site, Twin Stripes Camp Site and Lees Ferry Camp
Site.

This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Ferry Swale Canyon, Cave Canyon, Ninemile Draw, Salt Water Wash,
Fall Creek, Cathedral Wash, Colorado River, Honey Draw, Seven Mile
Draw, Water Holes Canyon, "5- Mile Wash", Paria River, Jackass
Creek, Badger Canyon and Soap Creek.
properties.instruction:
Flooding of washes and creeks will occur, some dirt roads will become
muddy and impassable. Paved roads and underpasses could become
flooded as well.

Get out of washes and creeks if you are camping or hiking! Flooding
is occurring or imminent and will inundate creeks and washes.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued August 30 at 9:10AM CDT until August 31 at 1:00PM CDT by NWS Indianapolis IN
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Indiana...
Illinois...

Wabash River at Riverton

.Minor flooding continues on the Wabash River at Riverton. The river
has crested. Flooding is expected come to an end on the Wabash later
tonight.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring.

* WHERE...Wabash River at Riverton.

* WHEN...Until late Sunday night.

* IMPACTS...At 16.0 feet, Some agricultural lands underwater.  A few
rural roads in Crawford County, Illinois close as water backs up
Minnow Slough.  High water affects campground at Leaverton Park in
Palestine.  A few private roads near the Gill Township levee in
Sullivan County may flood.  Water level is at the top of most
makeshift levees.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:00 AM CDT /9:00 AM EDT/ Sunday the stage was 16.6 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 10.5 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage just
after midnight tonight and continue falling to 4.7 feet
Wednesday, September 09.
- Flood stage is 15.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/ind.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 915 PM CDT /1015 PM
EDT/.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued August 30 at 12:07PM MST until August 30 at 2:00PM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
FFWFGZ

The National Weather Service in Flagstaff has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The Antelope Creek basin in...
Coconino County in north central Arizona...

* Until 200 PM MST /300 PM MDT/.

* At 1207 PM MST /107 PM MDT/, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms
producing heavy rain over the Antelope Creek basin. Between 0.25
and 0.5 inches of rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of
0.25 to 0.5 inches are possible in the warned area. Flash flooding
is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding in and around the Antelope Creek basin.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
Antelope Creek basin.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Rattlesnake Canyon, Owl Canyon, Upper Antelope Canyon, Lower
Antelope Canyon, Porcupine Canyon, Mountain Sheep Canyon, LeChee
and Wind Pebble Canyon.

This includes the following slot canyons...
Upper Antelope Canyon, Lower Antelope Canyon, Owl Canyon, Rattlesnake
Canyon and Porcupine Canyon.

This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Antelope Creek.
properties.instruction:
Get out of Antelope Canyon and other area slot canyons immediately!
Deadly flash flooding is imminent or occurring!

properties.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued August 30 at 1:42PM MDT until August 30 at 2:15PM MDT by NWS Billings MT
properties.description:
SVRBYZ

The National Weather Service in Billings has issued a

* Severe Thunderstorm Warning for...
Central Powder River County in southeastern Montana...

* Until 215 PM MDT.

* At 142 PM MDT, a severe thunderstorm was located 9 miles northwest
of Broadus, moving east at 45 mph.

HAZARD...70 mph wind gusts and small hail.

SOURCE...Home Creek Divide DOT reported a 65 mph wind gust at 1:30
PM MDT.

IMPACT...Expect considerable tree damage. Damage is likely to
mobile homes, roofs, and outbuildings.

* Locations impacted include...
Broadus, Biddle, Olive, Sonnette and Moorhead.
properties.instruction:
Anyone outdoors should move to shelter inside a well-built structure
and stay away from windows.

Wind damage with this storm may occur before any rain or lightning.
Do not wait for the sound of thunder before taking cover. Seek
shelter immediately inside a sturdy structure and stay away from
windows.
